content.text: In a recent In-Situ simulation held at the operating theatre, CIME introduced Victoria, a high-fidelity birthing simulator, for the first time. The session unfolded unexpectedly when a routine day turned into a critical scenario, testing the team's response to a gynaecological emergency.

The simulation began with a Code Blue alert for Victoria, who had just experienced cardiac arrest post-birth. Amidst the urgency of the situation, the medical staff swiftly sprang into action, demonstrating exceptional teamwork and clinical expertise in stabilizing Victoria.

The intense scenario not only provided a realistic test of the team's emergency response skills but also underscored the critical role of simulations in refining hospital protocols. Behind the scenes, the sim team meticulously orchestrated the session, ensuring an authentic and immersive experience for all participants.

By simulating real-world emergencies like never before, CIME continues to push the boundaries of healthcare education, preparing healthcare professionals to respond effectively to the most challenging situations.
